title: Mexico Captures 'El Chapo Isidro,' an FBI Top 10 Fugitive, in a Firefight That Killed 11

content:
Mexican military forces captured one of the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted fugitives on Friday night, Nov. 20, in the city of Guasave, Sinaloa — ending a manhunt that had lasted more than a decade.

Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, 44, known as “El Chapo Isidro,” was arrested along with seven other people, including his cousin Germán, known as “Serafín,” described as his second-in-command, and his brother-in-law José N, described as the cartel’s financial operator. Mexico’s Defense Ministry said the operation was carried out by elite military forces using “stealth and surprise,” with intelligence support from the United States.

Meza Flores was the 533rd fugitive placed on the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted list, added on Feb. 4, 2025. The U.S. State Department had offered a reward of up to $5 million for information leading to his capture. He was wanted on U.S. drug trafficking charges dating to a 2012 indictment, accused of smuggling heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl and marijuana into the United States for more than 20 years.

A night of gunfire in Guasave

The operation set off hours of violence. Mexican soldiers came under attack with gunfire and explosives as they moved in on the house where Meza Flores was hiding, and cartel gunmen set up flaming roadblocks across parts of the city. At least 11 people were killed in the fighting — four soldiers and seven suspected cartel members, according to Mexican authorities.

Gunfire sent baseball fans scrambling out of the stands at Kuroda Park stadium in Guasave during a Friday night game, and helicopters were seen firing on suspected cartel gunmen from above the city. Meza Flores was not flown out until 4 a.m. the next day, when he was taken to Mexico City aboard a Mexican Air Force aircraft.

Why it matters here

Meza Flores led the Meza-Flores Transnational Criminal Organization, also known as Los Mazatlecos, a high-ranking faction of the Beltrán Leyva cartel that controlled smuggling routes through Sonora and along the U.S.-Mexico border. His capture is the latest in a string of high-profile arrests and killings of suspected drug traffickers in Mexico, carried out under pressure from Washington. He awaits extradition to the United States to face drug trafficking charges.

Sources: Reuters, Nov. 21, 2026; CNN, Nov. 21, 2026; The Wall Street Journal, Nov. 21, 2026.
